To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the typology of clean technologies distinguishes four types with different capability requirements and innovation patterns, (2) the typology can be applied to anticipate the localization effect of clean technology deployment in countries with varying capabilities, and (3) the typology is a starting point for technology specific clean technology industry localization policies in developing countries and for international institutions to support green growth.

(1) there is no single 'best' policy to foster industry localization, (2) the effect of policies on industry localization depends on the capabilities required to produce the technology, the innovation pattern of the technology, the income level of the country, and the past deployment of the technology in the country, and (3) the heuristic can serve policymakers and international institutions as starting point for anticipating the effect of policies to foster clean technology industry localization in developing countries.

the localization of clean technologies in developing countries depends on the type of technology, the income level of a country, and the policy instruments used to promote the technology, and that the heuristic can help policymakers to anticipate the effect of different policies on the industry localization of different types of clean technologies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of which technologies are likely to be localized and how to anticipate the effects of clean technology industry policies.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the localization effects of clean technologies in developing countries depend on the type of the technology, on the income level of the country, and on the policy measures taken.
the effect of a policy on the development of a local clean technology industry depends on the type of technology, the income level of the host country, and the past history of the industry.
the effects of clean technology policies in developing countries are highly dependent upon the technology type and the income level of the country in question.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the localization of clean technology production in developing countries is a complex and multi-faceted process that requires the development of a broad range of capabilities and that is influenced by a number of factors, including past deployment policies, the stage of technology development, and the income level of a country.

the typology we developed and the heuristic we derived from it can serve as starting points for policy makers to anticipate the localization effect of different types of technologies and to develop green growth strategies that are tailored to the needs and capabilities of the country they are applied to.

the localization of a clean technology industry in developing countries requires the presence of a local market, the existence of a supportive policy regime, and the availability of a local supply of capabilities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the localization effects of clean technologies are not a given, but depend on technology specific factors.
the localization effects of green growth policies in developing countries are highly technology and country specific.
the localization effect of green growth policies depends not only on technology characteristics but also on the level of development of the recipient country.
